k2_results.kshape_bin: 1648 bytes = header 64B (int32 group[8] first-index = (0,1,3,9,21,35,49,62); int32 numElements[8] = (1,2,6,12,14,14,13,4) sum 66) + 66 entries x 24B. Entry = 20-byte occupancy array over a 5-wide x 4-tall grid (THE DECK GRID) + 4 ignored bytes. Lookup: 64 + (group[g]+elem)*24.

koma_record_MAP.0x0 u16 ImageId: CONFIRMED - 0..889, ALWAYS equals record index, fully redundant
koma_record_MAP.0x2 u16 characterId: CONFIRMED - 1..312, 312 distinct, each has exactly ONE 1-cell helper => 312 characters
koma_record_MAP.0x4 u8 seriesIdx: CONFIRMED - 1..42 into Koma.NameTable (src/JUS.Tool/Graphics/Koma.cs:33, from ARM9 0x0209E840). idx1="es" Eyeshield21, idx23="db" DragonBall, idx24="na" Naruto
koma_record_MAP.0x5 u8 panelOrdinal: CONFIRMED - panel number WITHIN THE CHARACTER (0-based), NOT char-within-series. (seriesIdx,panelOrdinal) unique across all 890
koma_record_MAP.0x6 u8 panelType: CONFIRMED - 0=Battle 1=Support 2=Helper; perfectly determined by size, zero exceptions
koma_record_MAP.0x7 u8 abilityId: PLAUSIBLE - range depends on type: helper 47 distinct in 0..55, support 193 in 0..192, battle 74 in 0..73 (74 == chr_b.bin entry count, so battle indexes chr_b)
koma_record_MAP.0x8 u8 KShapeGroupId: CONFIRMED - SIZE = value + 1 (verified by counting nonzero footprint cells: group g always yields exactly g+1 cells)
koma_record_MAP.0x9 u8 KShapeElementId: CONFIRMED - which shape of that size
koma_record_MAP.0xA u8 unkA: UNIDENTIFIED - 0..8, always <= size; == bbox width 474/890, == bbox height 500/890, neither exact
koma_record_MAP.0xB u8 flags: PLAUSIBLE - bit 0x10 ~= "primary variant". Values 0x00,0x01,0x10,0x20,0x21,0x30,0x31,0x32,0x42. NOT nature.

hp_structural_lead.observation: Naruto size-4/5/6 panels all share abilityId 20 (byte 0x7) yet have different HP, and koma.bin has no HP field.
hp_structural_lead.implication: Same structural signature as the nature gap. Either HP is computed at runtime from base stats + size, OR there is a per-panel stat table keyed by koma index - which would also be the natural home for nature.
hp_structural_lead.why_it_matters: Option 2 would resolve the nature gap and the HP gap with one discovery. Prioritise finding a per-panel table over hunting a nature byte.
